title: Held sources: field change, mutual cost and its sign

key_results.statement: Field operator with held sources: $C_f(g_1,g_2)=C_f+g_1\Phi_{x_1}+g_2\Phi_{x_2}$, the restriction of the total contract to a joint eigenspace of $(G_1,G_2)$ with eigenvalues $(g_1,g_2)$.
For every field start and every body start in one joint eigenspace of $(G_1,G_2)$, the bodies stay in their start and the field evolves by $e^{-iC_f(g_1,g_2)\lambda}$, exactly for all $\lambda$.

For a body start with components on several joint eigenspaces, (3.3) holds branch by branch and the field view is $\sum_g\lVert\beta_g\rVert^2\lvert\varphi_g(\lambda)\rangle\langle\varphi_g(\lambda)\rvert$, in general not pure.

In the starts of (3.3) the cost is exactly $\langle C_f\rangle_\varphi+g_1\langle\Phi_{x_1}\rangle_\varphi+g_2\langle\Phi_{x_2}\rangle_\varphi$ and conserved; a field start independent of the sources carries no mutual term at any order.

Response function of a non-degenerate eigenvector: $\chi_n(x,y)=\langle\varphi_n\vert\Phi_xQ_n\Phi_y+\Phi_yQ_n\Phi_x\vert\varphi_n\rangle$ with the reduced resolvent $Q_n$; real, symmetric, independent of phases, of the basis in other levels and of shifts $\Phi_x\to\Phi_x+c_x\mathbb 1$.
For non-degenerate $\varphi_n$ and $v<\Delta_n/2$: $E_n=e_n+\sum_i(g_i\bar\Phi_n(x_i)-\tfrac12g_i^2\chi_n(x_i,x_i))-g_1g_2\chi_n(x_1,x_2)+O(v^3/\Delta_n^2)$.
Second-order self terms $\Sigma_{n,i}=-\tfrac12g_i^2\chi_n(x_i,x_i)$ and mutual term $W_n=-g_1g_2\chi_n(x_1,x_2)$.

In the adapted eigenvector source $i$ changes $\langle\Phi_y\rangle$ by $\delta N^{(i)}_n(y)=-g_i\chi_n(y,x_i)$ up to $O(\lVert\Phi_y\rVert v^2/\Delta_n^2)$, reciprocally; from the unadapted start $\varphi_n$ the $\lambda$-average of $\langle\Phi_y\rangle$ equals this to the same order, while its cost stays (3.5).

For a level of multiplicity $d_\ell\ge2$ and $v<\Delta_n/2$, the $d_\ell$ branches are, up to $O(v^3/\Delta_n^2)$, the eigenvalues of $H_\ell(g)=\epsilon_\ell P_\ell+P_\ell VP_\ell-P_\ell VQ_\ell VP_\ell$.

For $d_\ell=2$ with $[P_\ell\Phi_{x_1}P_\ell,P_\ell\Phi_{x_2}P_\ell]\neq0$, each branch $\epsilon_\ell+g_1\alpha_1+g_2\alpha_2\pm\lvert g_1\vec a_1+g_2\vec a_2\rvert+O(v^2/\Delta_n)$ depends on both sources at first order, non-additively and non-differentiably at $g=0$, so it has no mutual term $\propto g_1g_2$; control: commuting compressions.

The sum of the branches of a level is analytic, with mutual term $-g_1g_2\chi^{(\ell)}(x_1,x_2)$ and level response $\chi^{(\ell)}(x,y)=\operatorname{Tr}[P_\ell(\Phi_xQ_\ell\Phi_y+\Phi_yQ_\ell\Phi_x)]$.

For weights $p(e_n)$: $\chi_\rho(x,y)=\sum_{e_n<e_m}\frac{2(p_n-p_m)}{e_m-e_n}\operatorname{Re}(\langle\varphi_n\vert\Phi_x\vert\varphi_m\rangle\langle\varphi_m\vert\Phi_y\vert\varphi_n\rangle)$, second order, $v<\Delta_{\min}/2$.

Sum rule: $\sum_n\chi_n(x,y)=0$ for all $x,y$, and the same over the eigenvectors in any subspace invariant under $C_f$ and all $\Phi_x$; exactly, the sum over all branches has no mutual part at any order.

If $UC_fU^\dagger=-C_f$ and $U\Phi_xU^\dagger=\epsilon_x\Phi_x$: $E_{U\varphi_n}(g_1,g_2)=-E_n(-\epsilon_{x_1}g_1,-\epsilon_{x_2}g_2)$ and $W_{U\varphi_n}=-\epsilon_{x_1}\epsilon_{x_2}W_n$; the ends of the spectrum have opposite mutual terms if $\epsilon_{x_1}=\epsilon_{x_2}$, equal ones otherwise.

For weights non-increasing (non-decreasing) in $e$, $[\chi_\rho(x,y)]$ is positive (negative) semidefinite, the self terms are $\le0$ ($\ge0$) and $W_\rho^2\le4\Sigma_{\rho,1}\Sigma_{\rho,2}$, second order; the bound can fail for interior eigenvectors.

$\chi_\rho(x_1,x_2)=\sum_{k<L}(p_k-p_{k+1})S_k$; $W_\rho$ has one weak sign for all non-increasing mixtures iff the partial sums $S_1,\dots,S_{L-1}$ have one weak sign, and non-decreasing mixtures then have the opposite sign; the ordering alone does not fix the sign.

A non-degenerate eigenvector sharp at $x$ has $\chi_n(x,\cdot)=0$; if sharp at $x_1$ and $x_2$, $E_n=e_n+g_1N(x_1)+g_2N(x_2)$ exactly and the field changes only by a phase; $\chi_n\equiv0$ if sharp at all $x$.

A field state that stays sharp at $x_1$ and $x_2$ along its evolution is changed by the sources only by the phase $e^{-i(g_1N_1+g_2N_2)\lambda}$, for all $\lambda$: a field state cannot stay sharp at the places of both bodies and respond to them.

At second order $W=g_2\delta N^{(1)}(x_2)=g_1\delta N^{(2)}(x_1)$ and $\Sigma_i=\tfrac12g_i\delta N^{(i)}(x_i)$; for an extreme non-degenerate eigenvector $\chi_n(x_i,x_i)=0$ iff it is sharp at $x_i$, and then $W_n=0$.

Three-place field $C_f=\omega(\lvert2\rangle\langle2\rvert-\lvert0\rangle\langle0\rvert)$, $\Phi_{x_{1,2}}=\lvert0\rangle\langle1\rvert\pm\lvert2\rangle\langle1\rvert+\text{h.c.}$: the interior eigenvector has zero self terms and mutual term $4g_1g_2/\omega$.

For every field and $x_1\neq x_2$, at second order, either all level responses $\chi^{(\ell)}(x_1,x_2)$ vanish or both signs occur among the levels: the sign of the mutual cost of like sources is never fixed by $C_f$ and the $\Phi_x$ alone, except when it vanishes in every level; the state fixes the rest.

Three-place chain with $\Phi_x=\lvert x\rangle\langle x\rvert$: $\chi_3=-\chi_1$, $\chi_2=0$; for like sources $W=2u,3u$ (neighbouring, end places) in the lowest and $-2u,-3u$ in the highest eigenvector, $u=g_1g_2/(16\sqrt2t)$; sign and neighbour-minus-end difference both reverse.

definitions.name: gap of the level of an eigenvector

open_issues: The zero of G_i is a convention (M6): the shift G_i → G_i + c, C_f → C_f − cΦ_{x_i} leaves C and the exact spectrum unchanged but changes the reference eigenvectors and the split into self and mutual terms; to be settled with 02-what-a-body-presents.
No relaxation (A11): what brings the field into an adapted state is open; in unadapted starts the cost has no mutual term (3.5).
Dependence on distance, whether the mutual term vanishes for far-apart sources, and hence which reading of the sign applies, belong to 04-profile.
For degenerate levels only level sums carry an analytic mutual term; orders above the second are not treated except in the exact results.
Mixtures are realised through an added object without contracts, an extension of the setting.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions of every term of (3.7), and g_2 = 0 gives the one-source expansion
Two-place field: exact eigenvalues reproduce self and mutual terms of (3.7), the sum rule (3.14), the end relation (3.15) and equality in (3.16)
Φ_x commuting with C_f: χ_n = 0 and (3.7) equals the exact eigenvalue, as in (3.18)
